member of the commission. − mr president, some weeks ago, as you remember, we discussed the contribution of taxation and customs policies to the lisbon strategy of growth, jobs and competitiveness. cross-border loss relief is one key element for establishing a competitive internal market without obstacles and thus contributing to growth and employment. let me explain the importance of granting cross-border loss relief for the internal market. imagine a small or medium-sized enterprise which is operating successfully in its domestic market. once it plans to expand its operation to other member states, to the internal market, it will not only run into problems regarding additional compliance costs. thus, in many cases, this sme will not be able to set off any start-up losses against profits which it may continue to generate in its member state of residence. the non-consideration of foreign losses results in double taxation and discourages many smes from investing in other member states. with the new initiative on cross-border loss relief, large enterprises – but also smes in particular – could more easily extend their activities abroad and enjoy the full benefits of the internal market. the initiative on cross-border loss relief constitutes a targeted solution in the short to medium term and represents an intermediary step. but please note that this initiative could in the future be complementary to the common consolidated corporate tax base (cctb), notably for companies that are not covered by the cctb. the initiative on cross-border loss relief is more limited in scope than the consolidation of the tax base under the cctb would be, as this provides automatic and comprehensive off-setting of all profits and losses within a group of companies. i highly appreciate the strong support expressed in ms kauppi’s report for the commission’s initiative in the field of cross-border loss relief, for the coordination approach and of course also for our work on the cctb. like you, i am persuaded that we should continue our efforts to dismantle tax barriers in the internal market.

of greater relative benefit to the small and medium-sized enterprises than the big multinationals. however, i understand the concerns, and to respond to the question at the end of the debate, i want to tell you that in the council it is on the table, but not as a concrete proposal. for the time being it is on the table as a concept, and as far as the concept is concerned, some two thirds of cross-border loss relief issue, would be premature because there is, for the time being, no concrete legislative proposal. in the legislative work programme of the commission, however, there is one point which states that, in the second half of the year, we will present a concrete legislative proposal – with the necessary impact assessment – on the ccctb. then we can discuss whether the concerns are relevant or not. one more point: if there is no unanimous agreement – and for the time being i believe that there will be no unanimous agreement – we can resort to enhanced cooperation as a solution. so, no single member state would be forced to accept the ccctb and to use it. and, even in those countries that chose the ccctb, no companies would be forced to use it, because there would be no sense in forcing companies that are not operating in the internal market – that are not doing business in the internal market – to use this common tax base. they can stay with the domestic national base used previously. so i share your conclusion that, in order to promote coherent development and the proper functioning of the internal market, obstacles deriving from the existence of different company tax regimes in the member states must be tackled, preferably through common approaches and coordinated actions. with regard to the loss offset, your report highlights several the application of anti-abuse measures in the area of direct taxation. the commission shares the concerns about tax avoidance expressed in your report. member states need to be able to prevent their tax bases from being eroded because of abuse and aggressive tax planning. at the same time it is vital to ensure that there will be no undue restrictions to the treaty freedoms. by launching this latest initiative, the commission seeks to prompt further discussions with the other institutions on how national anti-abuse measures can meet those requirements. your observations on tax avoidance the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank my colleagues, first of all, for their valuable cooperation, and in particular vice-president frattini for his commitment to the defence of children's rights since the beginning of his mandate. the report does not claim to cover all the issues, of course, but i think it is a good starting point. the aim was to lay the foundations for a strategy to promote and safeguard the rights of children in both the internal and external policies of the european union and to support the efforts of the member states in this area. the committee on legal affairs and citizens' rights has also called for the establishment of a european court of justice for children. the strategy aims first and foremost at affirming the positive rights of children, including the right to a family, the right to health, education, social inclusion, but also the right to entertainment, play, sport, as well as the right to a clean and protected environment. the aim is to create a child-friendly society, where children can feel safe and have a role to play. the report therefore rests on two main premises: 1) active participation of children in decisions affecting them; 2) mainstreaming, i.e. the integration and promotion of children's rights in all eu policies. in short, children's rights must finally become a political priority for europe, also because children represent about 30% of european citizens and there is still a lot to be done for them, starting with the fight against violence and abuse, with worryingly growing phenomena such as paedophilia and child pornography on the internet. the general objective is to ban all forms of violence, including so-called traditional practices, honour killings, forced marriages and not only the certainty of punishment for perpetrators of violence, but also a prevention strategy to support children at risk. another priority is the fight against child poverty. it is worth recalling that even within the european union 19% of children live below the poverty line and that it is therefore necessary to provide for appropriate support measures also to support their families. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of children against the dangers of drugs and the use of drugs in the context of the fight against aids. another key element of the strategy is to ensure education and training for all children, including the poorest and most disadvantaged. measures should also be taken for disabled children to avoid any form of discrimination. we are among the experts and therefore it is perhaps superfluous to list here all the emergencies to be dealt with: the report also highlights the need to address the problem of child labour, the proliferation of violent video games, the rise in international child abduction, the complexities of bureaucracy that make international adoptions difficult, the plight of child soldiers, child labour, the lack of registration of births, the staggering number of missing children who are no longer known. and you could go on and on and on. in fact, it is necessary to network appropriate tools and timely information to exchange successful experiences and good practice, to put in synergy links, including legal and criminal instruments, to deal with problems concretely and in real time, possibly succeeding in preventing them. i would like to conclude, mr president, by saying that with the adoption of the treaty of lisbon they have a few more chances. the charter of fundamental rights of the european union is now part of the treaty and therefore also article 24, which expressly regulates the rights of the child, thus establishing a legal basis for the implementation of the strategy. at this point not only parliament but above all the member states must get down to work immediately.
i would like to thank mrs angelilli for her sensitive work on a very important subject: the question of the future of the european union. a society that is hospitable to children is hospitable to all its citizens. i also believe that we are taking a very important step today in this parliament because the institutions which are able to deal with the situation of children will certainly be able to deal better with all european citizens. i believe that mrs angelilli's report contains many interesting and dynamic points which also provide the commission with guidance for the future steps ahead. i think there are some points that need to be made, particularly the need to be very careful about the figures of unaccompanied minors in administrative detention centres for migrants. the european parliament's committee on civil liberties, in its inspections of these places, has found that in many countries, in france, in belgium, in italy, many unaccompanied minors, many children are locked up in these places, in inhuman and degrading conditions, unacceptable for children as well as unacceptable for all men and women. we therefore believe that this point must be stressed and that attention must be paid to the need to prevent child labour. child labor is often linked to exploitation and is linked to poverty. for these reasons, we think that a contribution which must come from this parliament is a broad contribution which goes in the direction of improving the social conditions of the european union.

press, a direct cause of the present crisis seems to be the inaction and lack of will to adopt the measures required to solve the chronic problem of waste management. when the commission was first informed of the critical situation of the waste collection and disposal system in campania in spring 2007, it initiated infringement proceedings against italy for breach of community waste legislation. since then, the commission has been closely monitoring developments and has already carried out a first on-the-spot assessment of the situation, at the invitation of the italian government. a further meeting with the competent italian authorities is scheduled in the coming days. it is now up to the italian authorities to take immediate action to remove the garbage from the streets. but as this new crisis shows, it is not enough to simply remove garbage from the streets. any short-term measures must be complemented by the adoption, and most importantly, the effective implementation of long-term strategic measures. for example, an adequate network of waste treatment plants in full compliance with the standards laid down in community legislation. this should be combined with an integrated long-term waste management strategy aimed at promoting recycling and sorting of waste at collection. legislative decree no 61, adopted in may 2007 to resolve the waste crisis, has not achieved its objective. the emergency plan announced by prime minister prodi on 8 january is a more ambitious step in this direction, but the timetable of measures, which must be short and effective, remains crucial. we will continue to closely monitor the practical implementation of the measures by the italian authorities. the commission will continue to put pressure on the italian government to bring the crisis to an end and intends to pursue legal proceedings against italy. the continuing violations of community environmental legislation in campania must be brought to an end, as community law requires. although the situation appears to be difficult, it is not impossible for the italian authorities to comply with community waste legislation. i am sure that useful examples can be drawn not only from other member states but also from other regions of italy where solutions have been found for the controlled disposal of waste by combining various forms of reduction, collection and disposal.

author of the book. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the matter under discussion tonight has been discussed in depth, more than once, in fact, in the committee on justice, which i have the honour of chairing, and the same committee has instructed me, through this question, to have a debate, to have a discussion with the commission. this is the status of the european parliament elected in poland, which has an exception to elections and all the rules concerning elections to other parliaments in other member states. the elections to the european parliament in poland are governed by the act of 23 january 2004, which lays down the eligibility requirements in article 9: 21 years old to be eligible to stand until the day of the vote, no criminal record for intentional crimes, residence in poland and a number of other requirements. chapter 17 of the same law provides for the circumstances in which a member of the european parliament in poland may lose his seat: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. on the basis of a series of combinations, as we lawyers say, a member of the european parliament loses his seat automatically - that is, a member of the european parliament automatically decays - if he is the subject of a criminal judgment which has been passed, but as regards members of the polish parliament, the law of 12 april 2001 - both for elections to the sejm and for elections to the senate of the republic - does not provide for such a provision, so we are faced with a regulation which concerns in particular the polish member of the european parliament and not the national deputy in poland. for this reason we have discussed and asked ourselves a question, one of which has implications for the immunity request, and as you know, we have - and as commissioner frattini knows better than i do - the power to decide on this question. it is clear that if a member is automatically deprived of immunity in respect of a case in which immunity cannot be defended, there is an additional problem, an additional perplexity. for this reason, we ask, i ask on behalf of the committee, the commissioner whether he does not consider that the polish legislation on the election of the national parliament violates article 10 of the protocol on privileges and immunities, which provides that for the duration of the sessions of the european parliament, members shall enjoy on the national territory the immunities accorded to members of the parliament of their country. and so there is a clear contradiction where the loss of a seat as a member of the polish parliament is therefore foreseen, without any provision for the same treatment for members of the national parliament. but i also ask the commission whether it intends to bring an action before the court of justice to have poland amend this legislation and apply the treaty correctly, because we see a diversity and a contradiction with the treaty. i would like to ask the commissioner whether he can answer these two questions and whether he can find a solution to the problems i have mentioned.

member of the commission. - mr president, i have to say something. let me summarize this again. it was a very interesting debate and we all see very clearly the need to react here. i understand that you all want a quick response. i can tell you that there is also a directive, namely directive 2000/43/ec, which already guarantees the application of the principle of equal treatment without distinction of race or ethnic origin in the areas of employment, social affairs, education, access to and supply of goods and services, and which also applies to roma. i think that is also important here. this directive then also makes positive measures possible in the member states. it is true, however, that the member states are not obliged to incorporate those measures into their national legislation. but european legislation must be applied and i can say that we as the commission are determined to ensure that it is. the commission has therefore initiated infringement proceedings last year against 22 member states which have failed to implement european rules properly, including, mr agnoletto, italy. the european social fund is also our main instrument for integrating people into the labour market. a substantial part of the measures aimed at improving the employability of roma can be co-financed by this european social fund. for example, between 2000 and 2006, some €275 million went to projects specifically targeting roma integration. the high-level expert group on the integration of ethnic minorities has highlighted that certain esf-supported projects, such as acceder in spain, are exemplary in terms of effective roma integration. i would therefore like to make a further urgent appeal to the national authorities to make use of this possibility. i agree with mr swoboda that it is not only the national bodies, but also, of course, often the local bodies that play an important role here. the social exclusion of roma is indeed - as we all know - a complex phenomenon, which requires a unified approach to tackle, including all the important aspects of roma life: education, employment, health, housing, infrastructure. this approach requires effective coordination at the level of the european institutions. i am convinced that with these measures we will make real progress next year. i have heard, of course, that some of you - not all of you - would like to have your own commissioner to deal with this issue, and i will of course pass this on to my colleague mr špidla. but these are very different issues, so i think the most important thing is good coordination. the other question will certainly be discussed with mr špidla again. i would like to make a few brief remarks on some of the points which were raised in the debate. the first is the question of dialogue with civil society and with the roma themselves. i believe that such a dialogue is very important - the agenda includes the recommendation for the second reading by the committee on transport and tourism on the completion of the community postal services market (13593/6/2007 c6-0410/2007 2006/0196 ((cod)) (rapporteur: markus ferber) (a6-0505/2007).
the chairman of the council. - it is a great honour to be here today, at your plenary session. the commission's proposal for a directive on the completion of the internal market for community postal services was one of the most demanding legislative proposals for the co-legislator in the last 15 months. when the commission presented it in october 2006, everyone expected a continuing disagreement and a lively debate within our institutions about the future of one of the oldest and most classic public services in europe. the european council also welcomed the commission's new approach to the issue of the european union's role in the world economy. from the outset, our institutions have defined in their discussions the common objective of avoiding populism and demagoguery and focusing on the essential parameters related to this issue, including the social aspects for postal workers and the sustainability of the financing of the universal service. as we know, the postal sector is facing structural change and must adapt to new economic and social conditions. the final stage of the completion of the internal market for postal services provides a unique growth opportunity for all operators involved. after all, citizens expect us to maintain and further improve the quality and efficiency of postal services for the benefit of all users, wherever they live. the opening of the postal market has been a success story so far. new players have entered the market, and new business opportunities have been seized not only by these new players but also by existing ones. new services for consumers have developed. it is self-evident that full liberalisation of postal services is a necessary condition for the sector's recovery and its survival in new forms of competition and alternative offers. the approach of our two institutions reaffirmed the fundamental principles of protecting quality, reliable and affordable services for all users and the prohibition of discriminatory barriers for new market entrants. at the same time, both the european parliament and the council recognise fundamentally different conditions in certain markets for postal services in the european union. therefore, the council, in its common position, decided on a common end date for liberalisation until the end of 2010, while allowing certain member states an additional transitional period until the end of 2012 to bring the new rules into force. in line with the basic principle of all previous postal directives, the principle of subsidiarity allows them to adapt the common rules to specific national circumstances and ensures that the postal market is supervised by an independent postal regulatory authority. ladies and gentlemen, at the end of this short speech, i would like to congratulate mr markus ferber and the rapporteurs from all the political groups involved, the shadow rapporteurs, for their contributions to our fruitful and constructive discussions. although we sometimes disagreed with some of their specific comments, i would like to recall that the council incorporated a large number of relevant amendments in its november 2007 common position, demonstrating its political determination, openness and constructive flexibility. in particular, i would like to highlight the good work of the commission throughout the codecision procedure and its commitment to effectively assist and guide the member states on all issues relating to the implementation of the new directive. tomorrow, ladies and gentlemen, you will take the final decision and reaffirm our common agreement in principle, as set out in the council's common position and the recommendation of the committee on transport and tourism of 19 december last year. we are confident that we have struck the right balance between the different objectives and have tackled the political challenges openly and sensitively, without compromising the legal security of postal service providers and consumers. ladies and gentlemen, thank you again for your good cooperation and for this text, which i hope will be adopted, and thank you for your attention.
member of the commission. − madam president, tomorrow the european parliament should take a historic decision that marks the end of a process launched more than 15 years ago. the third postal directive brings to a good end the well prepared gradual process of full market opening. what today appears a clear and obvious solution was far from uncontested when the discussion started. on 18 october 2006 the commission presented its proposals. intense and constructive negotiations in the institutions followed. it was eventually the european parliament, through its report at first reading of 11 july 2007, that paved the way for the compromise result in front of you today. many in this house have actively contributed to this important result, and – on behalf of my colleague commissioner mccreevy – i wish to pay tribute particularly to the rapporteur, mr ferber, and his fellow shadow rapporteurs from the other political groups who have shaped the compromise. the same goes for the finnish, german, portuguese and – last but not least – the slovene presidency. some remarks on substance: the text that is now on the table is balanced. it takes into account the interests of different political groups and member states. the commission’s proposal had envisaged an earlier date for market opening, confirming the target date set by the existing postal directive. two additional years is a substantial period. it will give all operators time to complete their preparations. it should not, however, lead to complacency. what is important for the postal sector, its customers, its operators and its employees is that there is a final and unconditional date for full market opening. the common position provides for fair conditions and requires us to do away with market entry barriers. a limited number of amendments have been tabled for tomorrow’s vote. mostly these are amendments that were already rejected by the committee on transport and tourism in december. as my colleague, mr mccreevy, observed at the time, these amendments do not bring added value for the internal market, for postal users, or for postmen and women. there is a momentum to finalise the process of postal reform. to sum up, the text in front of you is, on balance, good in substance, and, if you look at its main provisions, you will agree with me that it is faithful to our objective: real market opening not as an end in itself but as the means through which we pursue the broader objective of a high quality, highly efficient and sustainable postal sector adapted to the needs of the 21st century.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i too, like the other members, would like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur, mr ferber, on his work. it is a work which began long ago and during which we have had important moments of convergence and some moments of dialectical discussion. as far as my personal position is concerned, as is that of my group, there has never been a battle of principle, nor an ideological battle, against the idea of liberalization, which we welcome and support, but which is obviously aimed at confirming the guarantees which are indispensable for the provision of universal service. in the present proposal for a directive, as voted by parliament at first reading and then revised by the council, we believe that this guarantee exists in principle, although certain conditions will have to be specified, specified and detailed. we do not want to be the fools who, when the forest is pointed out, stop to look at the tree, but on competition, including on the tariff side, between the operator in charge of the universal service and the other individual services, and the right and duty to access networks, should have been on behalf of the pse group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr president of the council, mr vice-president of the commission, i think i can share the approach adopted by commissioner frattini in this debate. we must look to the future, we must see how we can manage the time ahead with a sense of responsibility and a shared commitment by all the european institutions. we believe that after years of debate on the area of freedom, security and justice, in which this parliament has critically noted the democratic deficit - such a sensitive area for the fundamental rights of citizens - we can welcome the signing of the new treaty which finally creates a european dimension in this area and which gives parliament full legislative powers also in the fields of judicial, criminal and police cooperation and immigration and residence policies. so my group also believes that, even at this delicate stage of ratification, no institution can ignore this fact, a situation which has changed on the whole. we know that it is not possible to anticipate the entry into force of the treaty tout court, but we believe that it would be a political mistake to continue working on highly sensitive issues, regardless of the democratic scope of the treaty of lisbon. for this reason, our group also believes that a joint effort by parliament, the council and the commission is needed to identify some of the most important dossiers, not to block their progress, of course, but to ensure that parliament can be consulted when the treaty of lisbon enters into force and to integrate these dossiers into the new institutional framework. i am thinking in particular of the important dossiers on which we have only been consulted so far, such as the proposal for a european pnr system, the proposal for a revision of the framework decision on terrorism, the directive on the entry of highly qualified workers and the directive on a uniform procedure for the entry of migrants for employment purposes. i have a few seconds, mr president, to express a worried assessment of what the council said about the return directive. we appreciate the council's willingness and cooperation, but we feel that there are some extremely sensitive points. one point in particular: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
i would like to thank the commission and the council for their willingness to reach an interinstitutional political agreement as soon as possible in view of the new developments which we are about to witness in the coming months. from january 2009 this parliament will be able to play an important role in the area of freedom, justice and security, especially in the need for european citizens to be able to exercise democratic control over the choices made within the area of freedom, security and justice of this european union. we believe that 2008 is a year of transition and that it should be lived as such by identifying certain priorities in the area of freedom, justice and security. i think we must move forward on issues we can no longer go back on, on which there is a need to insist. i think that we need to establish a common asylum policy by 2010 and to speed up the process of identifying this common policy. i also think that we must soon have a general plan on legal immigration and not just encourage the entry of skilled or highly skilled immigrants, but also draw up a plan which covers all those entering the european union area. i believe that we also need to insist on the free movement of men and women within the schengen area, thus taking advantage of the results achieved in 2007 and trying to make the most of these aspects. i think we also have to try to live 2008 as a year of evaluation on some choices that have been made. i am thinking in particular of two important issues. i think that a real assessment of the usefulness and effectiveness of the frontex agency is needed. it seems to me that an objective assessment can safely lead us to say that it has not produced the effects that were hoped for by the vast majority of this parliament and of the european citizens. i also think that we should assess the enormous amount of databases that exist in our landscape. all too often, exchanges of information are not useful and sometimes lost. i will conclude, mr president. i think we will probably have to make a final assessment of the return directive as well. it seems to me that we have reached a point of no return and we probably need to change our strategy: we need to think about a plan of action and legal immigration and then figure out how to kick out, deport and detain immigrants.

in writing. - i welcome the progress made at the bali conference, which, thanks also to the role played by the eu during the negotiations, has led to unexpected results. it was crucial to give a signal of unity, cooperation and responsibility at this juncture, so that negotiations could be started in the best possible way to set new emission reduction targets for the post-kyoto period (2012). in accepting the conclusions of the ipcc scientists, all participants recognised at political level that climate change exists, that it is anthropogenic in origin and that action must be taken by 2020 to avoid irreversible damage to the planet's climate. i hope that copenhagen in 2009 will mark the turning point in the fight against climate change by setting stringent reduction targets by 2020 for all industrialised and developing countries. it is clear that this new challenge will involve costs and inefficiencies which are difficult to justify unless, as i have said in previous speeches, we make the necessary and courageous choices, such as going back to nuclear power. non-action, procrastination and exhausting conferences would only lead to irreversible environmental damage.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i should like to begin by thanking commissioner kallas for his valuable cooperation with parliament during its work. i would also like to thank olaf, in the person of its director, mr franz-hermann brüner, for its constant support and for the fundamental and not easy work carried out, and finally all my colleagues for their valuable contribution, as well as the structures and institutions of all the countries which are cooperating with us in this difficult work and - if i may - in particular our italian financial guard, which is distinguished in this endeavour by its high level of professionalism. the problem of protecting the community's financial interests is a matter of primary importance, directly affecting us as states and as citizens, and must therefore be tackled with the firmness and determination it deserves. the resolution tabled here today seeks to give a concrete response to the alarming phenomenon of fraud in the community. the data collected ... (the president interrupts the speaker to call back some members who are disturbing the debate) thank you, mr president, we are talking about transparency and it also takes great civility. the resolution tabled here today seeks to give a concrete response to the alarming phenomenon of fraud in the community. the data collected are worrying: in the field of own resources, agricultural expenditure and structural operations, irregularities in 2006 amounted to a total of eur 1 143 million, compared with eur 1 024 million in the previous year. the statistics show us an ever-increasing number of irregularities. however, it is important to stress that a high number of irregularities does not necessarily correspond to a high level of fraud. it can also be an indication of the effectiveness of control mechanisms and of close cooperation between the member states and the commission. the commission rightly emphasised the importance of such cooperation in its 2006 annual report, both for prevention and recovery. to date, statistical data are based on heterogeneous national structures with very different administrative, legal and inspection systems. in particular, it is considered unacceptable that spain and germany do not transmit to the commission the information on irregularities detected in electronic format as required for all member states. the community rules and the obligations imposed by the fight against fraud must be transposed in the same way by the different countries. to this end, closer cooperation between the member states and the commission is essential for the protection of the community's financial interests, which must be regarded as common, that is to say, as being more important than the interests of individual member states. it is necessary to strengthen synergies between the supervisory authorities and local administrations in terms of coordination and exchange of information. maintaining the organisation and disbursement of finance at central level entails complex implementation mechanisms and increases the distance between those responsible for financing and the final beneficiaries. another key point raised in the report is the simplification of legislation. the 2000-2006 programming period has shown that overly complicated rules favour the commission of irregularities. finally, there is a slight improvement in activity and recovery, but recovery remains a problem which causes considerable damage to the community budget. in particular, the 39-month period between the reporting of the irregularities and the notification is considered unacceptable, as this delay makes recovery even more difficult, if not impossible.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking all the members for their words, and in particular mr bösch, whose previous work also formed the basis for my report. i would like to stress a few points. i am particularly pleased that the commissioner has taken the initiative of drawing up a report on the implementation of the budget for the european union. he pointed out an important point: the more difficult it is, the more complicated it is, the more difficult it is to read these regulations, the more organized crime, especially, and all forms of illegality can creep into these dark spaces. so simplification - and i would also like to say more - bringing the people who give the money closer together with those who receive it is another mechanism for making this clear, transparent and easy to understand. the problem of recovery is a real problem. the time is too long, the ability to punish those who cheat the european community must be guaranteed by forms of surety, by forms of guarantees as can be applied through the banks. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we believe that we have done a fundamental job with the cooperation of all and with the political will and commitment of all our colleagues. it is clear that cooperation, willingness and the desire to curb this phenomenon, which is extremely harmful to the european community, is a purely political matter. the absence of the council certainly does not make this easier, because its presence would also have been a chance to find out what the council thought. but parliament is absolutely united and solidary around these principles, and so we feel that we have achieved something positive which gives us hope for the future.

in writing. in this plenary session we discussed the so-called 'goods package', which provides for uniform rules for the marketing of products within the european union and reaffirms the principles of reciprocity. the european parliament is currently working to increase the efficiency of the ce mark (european conformity) because it provides guarantees on product safety and allows goods from non-eu countries to be identified. however, in recent years another mark has appeared that is almost identical to it in graphic terms, except for the spacing between the two letters, which, however, means something quite different: the commission has not received any comments from interested parties. the citizens are calling for measures and sanctions, as well as for increased customs controls, to prevent the european ce mark from being misused. the italian regions are suffering from widespread marketing of imported counterfeit products which, at first sight, appear to meet the requirements for their placing on the market. this is also due to the confusion caused by the similarity between the two marks. the regulation will allow goods to move more freely within the eu, increasing consumer choice and confidence and simplifying the sale of goods.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i support the dunn report. the aim of the proposal is to bring the current regulation (ec) no 515/97 into line with the community's new powers in the field of customs cooperation by strengthening cooperation and exchanges of data between member states and between member states and the commission. it is the legal basis for requests for assistance exchanged between the competent authorities to combat irregularities and fraud. despite the good results achieved so far, there are various reasons for amending the text, mainly because of the change in the context and the institutional balance. the aim is therefore to ensure more effective coordination at community level in the light of the new instruments provided for by european law, taking into account that at the time of the adoption of regulation (ec) no 515/97 there was still no article on customs cooperation in the treaty (articles 135 and 280).

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the application of community law is an essential part of the 'better lawmaking' agenda launched by the barroso commission. for a while it remained a sort of cinderella, lost between the fashion of impact assessment and that of cost reduction. today the commission has stepped up its efforts, thanks in part to pressure from parliament. this is a procedure which has been going on for years, and which in many cases is a kind of bureaucratic transaction, where one infringement is followed by another with little effect, but which remains an absolutely indispensable procedure. the numbers speak very clearly. to date, there are some 2,518 infringement procedures open in a wide range of areas, in particular in the field of the environment and the internal market. in addition, the european parliament receives hundreds, if not thousands, of petitions each year, often referring to specific cases of breaches of community law, in which the citizen feels powerless and therefore turns to parliament. the question is: what chance of being satisfied? the infringement procedure is described in the treaty in articles 226 and 228 and there is therefore little to be creative about. the rules in force condemn us to slow and cumbersome procedures where the most effective measure - the financial penalty - is rarely applied and only after a very long time, even decades. but much, much can be done and i thank the commission for having proposed over the last two years, and then last september with a specific communication, a series of measures which are analysed and evaluated in my report and on which i would like to make a few comments later. but first, let me make a point which i consider crucial in this debate, because enforcement can be a very political issue and can be a formidable tool for increasing the credibility and visibility of the community institutions. i would like to mention two concrete examples of the commission's somewhat different approach: the waste crisis in naples and the via baltica motorway in the rospuda valley in poland. the waste crisis in naples is the direct result of the repeated violations of virtually all community waste rules over the years. and in fact, italy has been the subject of numerous infringements over the years and the court has condemned italy on many occasions. but only now, after years and when the situation has become intolerable for everyone and impossible to hide, has the commission decided to punch the tables. the commission's visits are followed very closely and citizens who are complaining about illegal dumping announce on tv that they are sending petitions to the european parliament. but i wonder: couldn't you have done it sooner? could we really have taken a different approach to prevent this from happening? you could have! and that is what commissioner dimas did in the case of the rospuda valley in poland, which was in danger of being disfigured by a planned infrastructure of the baltic way, where for the first time the commissioner asked for a suspensive intervention of the court which was granted. this is a very important precedent that tells us something extremely clear: the commission can and must be tough and strict with the member states who pretend to do nothing and must use all the means that the democratic system allows it: the media and public opinion. one of the most important innovations the commission makes in the communication concerns a so-called new working method. we have expressed many concerns about this new method of working, which is essentially based on referring the matter back to the member state to which the complaint is lodged in order to try to resolve the problem. we have expressed these concerns, the commission has given us some assurances, which i hope we will be able to hear again today, but we will keep a very close eye on this issue and we really hope that on the question of infringement procedures, the issue of transparency, the possibility of using the name and shame for the member states and the joint work with this institution can lead to progress. mr president, at the end of the debate i will take two more minutes to finish my speaking time.

does not end here. quickly some points. i would like to comment on the question of priorities, which commissioner verheugen has raised. i think that this can indeed be a risky exercise, but it has not the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr vice-president of the commission, today we are celebrating the end of a process which began in september 2005. we have had to travel a long and sometimes difficult road, but in the end i feel that it was worth it. the safety of civil aviation is at stake. the regulation that we had in place, which we have in place to this day, was adopted in the emotional climate of the attack on the twin towers on september 11, 2001. it had its own trouble in its formation, but then approved to be applied, and in these years it showed successes, but also gaps and practical inadequacies. that's why we're here today to change it. the aim is to allow a more flexible response to technological, psychological and behavioural changes in the fight against terrorism, taking into account, of course, the experience we have had so far. security and its protection against terrorist attacks are obvious priorities, but they cannot be discussed in isolation. they need to be seen in a slightly more balanced context. the controls must be strict and efficient, but must not cause excessive inconvenience to passengers and must not entail unnecessary costs for their application. the costs must be shared wherever possible and not be borne solely by the passengers. that is why new controls cannot be introduced without proper democratic scrutiny. in short, these are the two points - costs and democratic accountability - on which parliament's delegation has focused its attention in the conciliation phase of this procedure. on costs i think i can be pleased to report to parliament that an article, not a recital, has been included to establish that they the costs of security must be shared between travellers, airports, airlines and national governments. a further article, not an interinstitutional declaration as it was in 2002, but an article obliges the commission to examine the problem in greater detail and to produce to this parliament and to the council proposals that solve it by a correct allocation of the same between taxpayers and passengers. on democratic accountability we have worked successfully to get the use of enhanced comitology or comitology with scrutiny, especially in the case of the introduction of any new checks, new controls, new possible limitations on the lives of passengers. in future, whenever parliament considers that the security measure is disproportionate to its purpose, it will have the opportunity to call for a public debate, to arrive at these considerations in an appropriate manner. in short, it seems to me that the balance between efficiency in the fight against terrorism and at the same time the widest possible respect for privacy, for behaviour, for unnecessary harassment of passengers, has been achieved in this way. of course, only the actual proof of its application will tell us whether this has been fully achieved. that is why, mr president, i feel i should recommend to this house, to our assembly, that we approve the agreement reached in conciliation and allow the commission to start its work effectively.

the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the report on european sustainable transport policy is now before the house. the text was already welcomed, without causing any major controversy, in the committee on transport in january. only about 40 amendments were tabled. i have set as my main objective for this own-initiative report to be succinct, developing no more than twenty paragraphs, so that the european parliament could put forward its recommendations to the commission and the council in the most effective way possible. the vast range of topics covered - european transport, energy and environment policies - development and an excessive number of paragraphs would have weakened the text and made parliament's final resolution less clear and incisive. for the same reason, some topics were left out. an own-initiative report cannot deal with and exhaust all the issues related to transport, energy and the environment. however, this document can be useful to the commission for future legislative proposals and to highlight what european citizens expect from the community institutions. i have received eight amendments for this final passage in the house. there is nothing new in the debate on the transport committee. i should like to make a few brief remarks on these points. the green group has tabled six amendments and has asked for a separate vote on paragraph 16. the latter request removes the reference to the use of nuclear electricity by rail transport and i cannot agree with that. rail transport is the lowest co2-emitting mode of transport, thanks also to the use of nuclear as a source of electricity. number 6 asks the commission to take action to set a single speed limit on european motorways for all countries. it has already been demonstrated on several occasions by our german friends that the motorways in germany are safer and that the number of accidents is lower than in many of the european union countries where there is a limit. the principle of subsidiarity should, of course, continue to apply in this case. i personally find amendment no 2 more coherent, in particular the first part on cost transparency in air transport and ticket prices. amendment no 8 was tabled by mr blokland on behalf of the independence/democracy group. this text refers to paragraph 2 and analyses the measures to be taken by citizens to improve urban and extra-urban mobility. in this case i must ask for a negative vote, because the amendment takes the opposite line to that taken in the text voted in the committee on transport. finally, my group has proposed an amendment to paragraph 11 of the report tabled by the committee on transport, which concerns the revision of the eurovignette directive. i was not and am not opposed to the possibility of speaking on this subject in the appropriate places in june. the european commission has already announced that it will be issuing this revision proposal at the same time. however, i think that, in line with what has already been proposed in the committee on transport, i would propose that we should be free to vote on the amendments in question. i thank all my colleagues for the interest they have shown in this report and in my work, and since i know that many others have asked to speak, i will leave it to them to do so.
the commission is therefore proposing to extend the period of validity of the directive to the period of 1 january 1999. the commission has already made a number of proposals. the report contains many good suggestions, but it is based on the assumption that ever-increasing traffic is a law of nature and that most problems can be solved by technology. i would like to emphasize two points in particular: the eurovignette is the starting point for calculating all transport costs, including external costs, because lorries are the means of transport which cause the greatest burden not only on transport infrastructure but also on people and the environment. even though commissioner barrot, responsible for transport, has promised that the transport protocol to the alpine convention will be ratified during the french presidency, i think that we should make an explicit reference to this protocol in the report. people talk about traffic all the time. but it is a fact that co2 emissions from transport in the eu increased by 32.1% between 1990 and 2005, aviation by 90%, while all other sectors were able to reduce the climate killer carbon dioxide by 9.5% in accordance with the kyoto protocol. we are too satisfied with lofty aims and pious wishes in this report. but it needs concrete guidelines and effective measures - including sanctions - or else everything will continue as the saying goes: 'the road to hell is paved with good intentions'.

declaration closing the 2007-08 session of the european parliament.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the main actions planned for 2009 are largely compatible with the lisbon strategy for growth and employment. the single market and competition certainly have some points which i support. there is certainly something to be said for a sustainable europe. unfortunately, the common visa policy is completely to be rejected, because in my view it is not only anti-national but also totally outside the mandate of this parliament and what our intentions should be. i am also absolutely opposed to enlargement to include croatia and turkey and even to a part of it that deals with kosovo, which i have already had occasion to condemn for the international lawlessness that has been committed when it was recognised as a state to the detriment of a sovereign country. that's why i'm voting against it.
member of the commission. − mr president, i should like to thank the house for a very interesting and supportive debate. although there was some criticism of lack of money or that we again want to establish something. i think the most important innovation starts with openness and promotion of creativity. the result of the consultation and legislative process is really an example of openness, contribution, commitment and even a creative innovative approach. we have shown innovation in coming to this consensus and also in the context and content of this result. this is the most important thing. the mission of the eit is, first of all, innovation. it is one of the moments or follow-ups of the lahti summit of october 2006 and actually we only proposed the draft text one day before the summit. we never supported green-field investment to establish something new; rather, we wished to come up with a new approach on how to promote, organise, motivate and mobilise resources and partners in order to make innovation in europe more successful. i would like to recall that the commission never had the option to build new buildings for the eit, but to come up with the new approach. it took one and a half years: we started it as a part of the lisbon strategy in february 2005 and since then we have had many coffees and many talks that were very inspirational and very interesting – also in this building – showing that there are a lot of options or opinions on how to promote innovation. i am happy now that we have come to this strong joint commitment. many people spoke of the location. this is an issue for the council. i think the slovenian presidency will try to manage the process leading towards a decision. names have been mentioned already – some at member state level. some cities at regional level are also aspiring to this. it is a good signal that there are many ambitious candidates for the seat of the eit. there are also many universities and businesses and research and technology organisations which are keen not only on the consultation process, but in participation in the selection of the governing board and then in the work of the eit. as ms hennicot-schoepges said, we are not going to lose identity; we offer to share the identity between universities or existing centres and the eit which is going to be established. that is more or less all i wanted to add as a response to your points and support. once again i want to underline the importance of convergent, horizontal work. as you did in this parliament in your committees, we did the same in the commission. i was not isolated. i am not alone. it was achieved with the support of the president, the industry commissioner, the research commissioner, the budget commissioner and many others. i think this is a very important message for the future: let us work together, be open-minded and promote creativity. this month i want to propose that we declare 2009 the european year of creativity and innovation. it will link strongly with the proposals, ideas and policies we need to nurture and establish in europe. once again, thank you very much. it is not a fait accompli; it is, rather, the beginning of the phase which means establishment, and then the real work may start – and i hope it will start successfully.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place today. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
president of the juri committee. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the rules of procedure require the european parliament to verify the credentials and to decide on the validity of the mandate of newly elected members. at its meeting on 25 february the committee examined the credentials of the 35 romanian members appointed by the competent authorities. these names must be supplemented by three others designated by the respective national authorities. in view of the large number of checks to be carried out and the limited time allowed, it was considered appropriate that the committee on legal affairs, and therefore its chairman, should inform parliament orally. the fact that the committee has recorded everything properly therefore gives the house the opportunity to ratify everything.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i shall vote in favour of the report by mr paolo costa on the draft common rules on civil aviation safety and repealing regulation (ec) no 2320/2002. i believe it is essential to create a simpler and more flexible legislative framework which increases the freedoms and decision-making powers in the legislative implementation phase compared to the previous overly detailed provisions. however, i think it is appropriate to make some distinctions, particularly as regards the link between airport charges and the costs of the services offered. in this context, i feel it is necessary to urge the commission to adopt as soon as possible provisions on the financing of security measures at european airports and the transparency of security costs, in order to deal with any distortions of competition in this area.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i welcome the report by mr paasilinna, who intends to contribute to economic growth and the competitiveness of the eu by developing new forms of innovation through the creation of the european institute of innovation and technology (eit). the eit aims to support the characteristic element of the level of competitive capacity: the "knowledge". the latter, by definition, cannot be a static concept, and can therefore only exist through a dynamic and structured process of research and new discoveries. the only way to achieve real progress is through innovation. today, the global market for the old and new 'knowledge economies' is dominated by competitors such as the united states, india and japan, which have always made innovation the key to economic development, and therefore enjoy a strong competitive advantage over the eu. the eit will therefore serve to strengthen the exchange of knowledge, to bring together, exchange and circulate ideas, to aggregate research from all over europe around macro-areas essential to the development of the eu's future competitiveness. the potential benefits to the competitive system of our market are almost limitless. it will be up to us to ensure that the 2.4 billion euro allocated is used properly and that the european union can face the future challenges of the world market with greater vigour.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, transport has an impact on the socioeconomic fabric of society and, at the same time, it has a direct impact on environmental issues. urban transport generates 40% of co2 emissions and makes europe dependent on and hostage to the market for fossil fuels such as oil, which accounts for about 70% of total demand. these alarming figures are enough to show the urgency and the need for a new overall transport strategy in europe, which could in fact be developed on the basis of this report. the pollution caused by transport must be reduced rapidly by restricting emissions of pollutants, by changing the composition of petrol mixtures and by continuing to encourage the purchase and use of environmentally friendly and non-polluting vehicles. the eu will therefore have a responsibility to implement an integrated plan to achieve this important objective, committing itself to incentivising rail transport which, when improved as appropriate, can ensure a high level of efficiency with a low environmental impact. the tens need to be completed quickly and require increased eu financial support. on the other hand, member states must ensure and supervise the construction of such works except in cases of proven environmental or health hazards.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to give my favourable vote to mr albertini's excellent report on a european policy for sustainable transport, taking account of european energy and environmental policies. i believe it is essential that the eu coordinates its policies in order to develop urban public transport and alternative transport systems, while protecting the environment and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. as regards infrastructure, i note a continuing emphasis on road projects at the expense of rail projects. the completion of the transeuropean networks still seems far off and the eu's contribution is minimal compared to what individual countries will have to do on their own. in order to reduce gas emissions and improve the efficiency of freight and passenger transport, i reiterate the need for the eu to provide financial support for the implementation of priority projects in the framework of the transeuropean networks.
on behalf of the uen group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, we are among those who believe and defend the continuation of the cap beyond 2012. we believe that this report is moving in the right direction, but we cannot accept that total decoupling of aid does not provide for the possibility of maintaining partial coupled aid for certain specific sectors in order to avoid total abandonment of production. there are entire supply chains, such as tobacco, which would disappear if total decoupling were applied, creating unemployment and various economic and environmental problems in particularly disadvantaged areas. we consider that the gradual modulation of aid is a measure which may be excessive and probably counterproductive if the objective is to safeguard european agricultural production. we recognize the importance of rural development, but we believe that it cannot be implemented at the expense of the first pillar of the cap. in addition, policies to support individual cmos should continue to be implemented where necessary. the european union, mr president and mrs commissioner, needs a common agricultural policy that succeeds ... mr president, ladies and gentlemen, madam commissioner, i thank the rapporteur for this very relevant report, given the complexity and the vast scope of the subject under discussion. i would like to stress two points which i consider particularly important. the first is that i consider the cap to be an important instrument which must be maintained after 2013 because it is a support for business. but that is precisely why it must be aimed at entrepreneurs, because it creates jobs, it maintains the environment, it guarantees high quality products. the second concerns the delicate question of milk quotas. i agree with the rapporteur that we need to protect those european regions where there is no alternative to livestock farming and milk production, but we must not forget all those farmers who have invested heavily in buying milk quotas and who could be in serious economic difficulties from 2015. i hope that a solution satisfactory to all can be found with the commissioner, also because in 1984, when the quota system was introduced, italy was against it and today it is still running a deficit of about 40% of the milk it consumes.

member of the commission. − mr president, i wish to begin by thanking everybody not only for supporting the proposal in the report but also, and even more, for supporting the smes. smes are a vital part of the european economy and here, as i have already said, in the eurostars programme we are talking about smes which will be the ‘stars’ of the future. this is an innovative approach. it is not easy to implement approaches where we combine money from the member states with community funding, but it is definitely worthwhile, because that is exactly the direction in which we should go in the future. we are joining the best of eureka – flexibility, simplicity, decentralised approach, market orientation – with the best of the framework programme: centralised management, common evaluation and common selection. i can assure you that also in the other parts of the framework programme we are keeping our eyes very much open for the benefit of the smes. simplification is the name of the game, so we have introduced, as you are probably aware, a higher funding rate for smes than for the rest. so they have a 75% co-funding rate in the framework programme, while the rest of the bigger companies have 50%, which means that we are stimulating their participation. we have introduced a guarantee fund, which very much simplifies their participation in the framework programme, because the fact that they have to submit some bank guarantees in advance was one of the major problems for smes; and we are also about to introduce a ‘unique registration facility’ which will again ease the job because you will have to apply only once and all your data will be stored and the next time you apply this will be done automatically. therefore, if we look at the results of the first year – and as you know, we agreed about the target of 15% funding which should go to smes from the cooperation part of the programme – we can say that it is working. while in framework programme 6 we were not achieving the target, from the first evaluations and first insight into the results, we can see that this figure is closer to 20% than 15%, which is a major step forward. we are also working in the commission. i have just come from a meeting of the competitiveness group where we discussed the small business act – that is the working title – where we want to address all the issues connected with smes in an organised way. i would also like to mention that, although today we are deciding about financial participation from the community side, in fact this has already begun, and more than 200 have applied for the first call, which is an important success. finally, i should like to mention that i am extremely glad that luxembourg has decided to join. there is definitely no problem in substance. we should all do our best to make its accession to the programme as quick as possible.

author of the book. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have a very clear view of the importance of finally systematically addressing the issue of adaptation to climate change in the european parliament, which, to be honest, we have so far underestimated in its importance. the opportunity provided by the commission's green paper to encourage us to look into this matter is therefore very important. we know that now. we are engaged in a very strong battle to do what we can to mitigate global warming and we are discussing a legislative package that should take a very important step forward in this commitment. and yet we know that the effects of climate change are already being felt in many parts of the world, especially in the poorest areas of the world and also in important parts of our continent and of our europe. we must therefore react and develop a suitable policy in this direction too, which is not at all incompatible with the priority action that must be taken, i repeat, in the field of emission reduction and the mitigation of global warming. i think that bali has made a very important step forward in this respect too, when it decided to finance the world environment fund by allocating these cdm quotas specifically to the financing of adaptation projects in developing countries. and i have seen, if i read correctly, that also in bangkok last week, in the first important meeting after bali, a work programme was set up which provides that in june in bonn, in the next meeting, the theme of adaptation will be the focus. i have taken up this aspect of the international dimension because, in drawing up the resolution which we adopted as the clim committee and which we are bringing to the house's attention, this aspect of international cooperation is my top priority: the european union is equipped to develop cooperation and financial and technical-scientific collaboration with the countries that need the most help, having less capacity to cope with the sometimes devastating effects of global warming that have already been produced. let's think about the pacific islands. we had a hearing where representatives of some of these realities came and explained to us the dramatic nature of their situation, already today. the other priority is of course careful calibration to maintain a dynamic interdependence between mitigation and adaptation. the third is a strong impetus for research and experimentation. the knowledge available is still insufficient to measure effectively, in the extreme variety of territorial situations, the effects of global warming and it is therefore difficult to set up long-term policies to adapt, to prevent the most worrying aspects. of course, the key point in the coming years, with a strong political will from all actors at all levels, will be integration with other policies. we have stressed above all the report, the rethinking that needs to be done to take account of climate change in cohesion policies, a rethinking that must also be carried out on the basis of the adaptation of agricultural policies and, more generally, land management. in this connection i think we should support the amendment which has been tabled to urge the council to finally adopt the common position on the soil protection directive. finally - and i think i have five minutes, mr president - i think it is very important to strike the right balance here too, between european policies and local action. we are, in fact, interpreting the principle of subsidiarity dynamically and not bureaucratically. the extreme variety of situations in europe means that a single policy cannot be defined. of course there are the areas of southern europe, there is the alpine belt, which have very different and very important effects. i think that the committees will have to establish a very close, two-way relationship with the regional authorities. i am thinking of large-scale regional experiences, such as the alpine convention or the carpathian convention, which are developing very important initiatives and which can also be taken as models to project them onto the international cooperation scene. i thank you, commissioner, and i hope you will tell us how the preparation of the white paper is proceeding, after the consultation on the green paper.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to say that this debate is the first outcome of the temporary committee on climate change, which we wanted to have as a venue for developing a system policy, because adaptation and mitigation are intimately linked. we are talking about adaptation specifically here, but we must not forget how we actually have to make sure that the resources for adaptation also come from trade, from the emissions trading mechanism. because it is the poorest countries that bear the greatest burden of climate change, we must ensure that the resources that come from the emissions trading complex are originally made available to developing countries. i believe that we can do this by adopting a general principle of equity, which is to give free emission allowances, which will then be established, essentially on the basis of a principle of equity, which is that of 'one person, one emission allowance'. and so you see, if we think about the poor 1.5 billion people in the world with the quotations that we now have in the current kyoto protocol, which are about 20 euros per ton, giving a carbon right of, say, one ton could make available to the poor people of the world 30 billion euros a year for mitigation measures. think, this could be what bangladesh needs to be able to do this minimal mitigation. some african states are already thinking in this direction and so this principle of equity also means that we are the main responsible for this phenomenon and that we take on the responsibility of also carrying out mitigation. in our area, we have a changing climate which means more intense rain, longer droughts and less snowfall. we must therefore carry out integrated maintenance of the land for soil protection, and i stress this importance in the speech by president sacconi, precisely because water, in situations of general scarcity, must be kept where it falls precisely because it feeds the groundwater. and longer droughts also mean more fire chances, which we can respond to by clearing the forest to extract a fire load. but it is a general effort which we must make with consistency and determination.
i believe that even if we were able to keep global warming within two degrees, this would still mean that europe would be facing a scenario of extreme climate change, with consequences for the local economy, the environment and the population. the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of life in the regions of the community, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for his report. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's climate change strategy and will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's climate change strategy. at the same time, we also need to invest in policies to ensure access to common goods, such as water, food and health resources in the most vulnerable areas. water is becoming an increasingly scarce resource and so there is a need for management that makes it available and accessible to all. finally, i want to conclude by saying that climate change adaptation policies cannot be separated from social equity interventions. a new model of economic development is needed that includes environmental costs and focuses on sustainability as a factor in employment development and new social policies.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to concentrate on two points. already today billions of people lack access to water, and hundreds of millions die as a result. climate change is bound to make this situation worse. the cost is particularly high for those continents, such as africa, which already suffer from terrible conditions and which, although they are the least polluting, suffer the most from climate change. the right to water must become a real priority of adaptation policies. i say 'right' because it has not been enacted yet. international documents speak of "water demand", and there are actual military and economic wars under way to appropriate water and to market it. it is therefore necessary to establish the right and to implement policies which will make it possible to make this right a reality. i think it would be useful to work on a protocol on water to be included in the documents of the post-kyoto agreements. and with water, the soil. we have a european directive that needs to be approved. desertification must be combated and the role of soil as a factor in climate balance promoted: that's our policy. good agricultural practices, as opposed to, for example, biodiesel production, can provide both food and co2 capture. adaptation, then, is not about surrendering to climate change but about taking action to combat it.
