the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i am very pleased to introduce this debate to you this evening, because it brings to a close a work which started with great difficulty but which i believe has achieved results of great importance. we are discussing very technical matters this evening, but they are matters which, in my view, contribute to the construction of europe much more than many of the talks we have with each other in many other places. we were not aware of it, but there are almost 700 000 railway wagons in europe which can now move from one country to another, which can be used by one company rather than another and which until now were prevented from crossing the frontiers with a certain amount of peace of mind, because we had not guaranteed common safety rules from one side to the other. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the safety of railway vehicles is not compromised by the introduction of new safety standards, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for his report. finally, we are beginning to see the single railway market which was envisaged in 1957 with the first treaty but which we have not yet achieved. the point we were working on in the proposal for a safety directive was to create a system of certification of the maintenance of railway wagons, which would be available not only to railway companies, not only to those who operate the infrastructure, but also, if necessary, to any third party who decided to invest in a wagon fleet. and this without discriminating, without eliminating the responsibility of the railway companies, in the use of the wagons themselves when they are moving. we have long discussed whether this certification should be voluntary rather than mandatory, whether we should limit ourselves to railway wagons rather than the rest of the things, and i think we have found a good solution. the commission has already made it clear that it will be compulsory for wagons for the next two years, and for other vehicles, passenger vehicles, within a decade. this system has been outlined, this path has been followed, and in a little while we will arrive at the point we are interested in. the regulation on agencies - i am particularly interested in emphasizing - is the point on the european signalling system, which allows a technological step forward and the possibility of eliminating other things. we had two problems: how can we ensure that the technological innovation we need to drive and keep growing does not leave us uncertain about where we need to go to invest in moving to this signalling system. well, i think that here too the solution has been found, which fixes a version 2.3.0 these days and brings it forward and is compatible with the fact that in 2012 we will have the even more advanced and final one that we will have to do. for these reasons, having solved - i think - brilliantly these two problems, i think i can recommend to parliament that it vote on the agreement reached at second reading, which also makes it possible to demonstrate efficiency in our work and in our relations with the council.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the excellent work of mrs sartori seems to be the ideal legislative outcome for updating and thus better regulating the treatment of chemicals. it is commendable that the report not only meets the united nations harmonisation programme but also appears to be consistent, taking into account the needs of producers and consumers and, of course, i would say the environment as far as is objectively possible. as usual, some of my colleagues are not satisfied, and i have the impression that this is due to an ideological radicalisation of technological and scientific progress which all too often, in the name of protecting the environment, seeks to coerce man. it is also the case that, for reasons radically opposed to those mentioned, those non-european states, china in particular, which, in the name of the absolute primacy of the economy, set up conditions for the production, transport and storage of chemical materials in gross disregard of everything that is rightly sought to be protected here, do the same. the sartori report is a major step forward in harmonizing the classification of substances and the labelling and packaging of dangerous substances and mixtures. this certainly contributes to improving safety and preventing hazards to the health and safety of consumers, workers and the environment. it is possible today for the same substance to be classified in a profoundly different way from one state to another, by virtue of the different classification system in force, with fluctuations which for the same substance are strongly and dangerously different. substances classified as dangerous in europe are, for example, labelled in china without any special precautions. this, in addition to giving unfair competitive advantages, represents a serious danger for all consumers, and this, ladies and gentlemen, is all the more true in an unfortunately global market.

on behalf of the alde group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we have worked on the joint motion for a resolution on maternal mortality, bearing in mind that objective 5 'reducing maternal mortality by 75% by 2015' is far from being achieved and requires a strong initiative, a strong and concrete initiative by the international community, of which the europe of rights and values can only be the interpreter and guarantor. we have noted the reassuring statements made by mr jouyet and mrs ferrero, but we must quickly move from statements to facts. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. as all of us remember, most of these women live in sub-saharan africa, where one death occurs every minute, and, as mentioned, the comparison with women living in the west for the same risk is 1 in 3,700. these figures are made all the more dramatic by the encouraging progress made in the same years by some middle-income countries in east asia, southeast asia, north america, latin america and north africa, showing that this repugnant situation can be overcome. the resolution is therefore, in our view, timely, articulate and comprehensive and identifies appropriate strategies to address this truly global health emergency, recognising that access to an adequate level of health care is a fundamental human right. in conclusion, i hope that the commendable compromise reached between the groups on such a divisive issue will find the widest possible convergence in the assembly and that the adoption of the joint resolution will urge all our institutions and every country to take concrete action and adequate investment in infrastructure and transport, health care, training of workers, education, prevention and policies for the emancipation of women, in order to achieve this important goal of civilization in 2015.
mr president, commissioner, mr president of the council, ladies and gentlemen, it is obvious that we must work to ensure that women can perform their maternal duties in the best possible health. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for his work. but i cannot hide the unease that comes from the international misuse of the term "reproductive health services": we want reproductive health services, but we cannot accept that they include voluntary abortion, so that it is transformed from the dramatic suppression of human beings at the dawn of their existence into a social service. i think that in a document on maternal health it should not be forgotten that motherhood is a two-person affair, not a one-person affair. i therefore find it very gratifying that the compromise resolution actually refers to both the declaration and the convention on the rights of the child, which also recognize the name of the child before birth and require special services from both the mother and the child. i therefore think it would be appropriate for the documents designed to ensure the safety of maternity to always mention, in addition to the other instruments already mentioned, those aimed at giving birth preference to abortion. this is solidarity, economic, social and psychological aid and education in respect for life. on the other hand, if you limit yourself to insisting on the use of contraception only, perhaps including abortion, you will not get the desired results. there are countries in europe, such as france and england, where contraception is certainly much more widespread than in other countries, and where, conversely, abortion is steadily increasing, as has been officially reported. i would simply ask my colleagues to give a little thought to these observations of mine.

member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should also like to thank mr bussereau for his continued commitment. i should like to go into the substance of the various reports and amendments which have been tabled. as regards the first vote, the report by mr sterckx on the monitoring of maritime traffic, i am very pleased that parliament has given its full support to the objectives set out in the commission's proposal. the most important provisions of the proposal are those concerning places of refuge. we fully support parliament's efforts to preserve the principle of independence in the decision-making process which allows the reception of a ship in distress in a place of refuge. the amendments which take up the substance of the proposal for a directive on mr kohlíček's report, civil liability and financial guarantees for shipowners, can be supported without reservations, with the exception of the two which refer to the establishment of a community office for the management of financial guarantee certificates. my services have doubts about the administrative and financial implications of this proposal, which we will have to examine in greater depth. on the other hand, i am pleased to read in mr kohlíček's report that parliament's support for the proposal on accident investigations is not diminished. the commission has also been sensitive to the argument raised in the council debate that in order to ensure the quality of investigations, it is necessary not to multiply them unnecessarily: what is important is that in addition to the cases of very serious accidents, an investigation be carried out so that lessons can be drawn from the understanding of the causes of the accident for the future. this objective, which corresponds to the imo solution, is guaranteed by the common position, so i cannot support amendments nos 7 and 13 or 14. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. while it is true that the commission proposal, as well as the common position, require member states to avoid conducting parallel investigations, it is also true that they do not deny the member states concerned the right to carry out their own investigations. in any event, it cannot be the commission's task to act as an arbiter between member states, each of which is convinced that it has an essential interest in carrying out an investigation. what is important in this case is to guarantee the independence of the investigating bodies. as regards compensation for passengers in the event of accidents, you know from the report by mr costa that the commission is determined to see the rights of passengers strengthened in all transport sectors and everywhere in europe. when the commission put forward this proposal three months ago, it had started from the following premise: if an accident happens in europe on board a vessel at sea or on a river, victims will not be adequately compensated because the applicable rules are too different from one member state to another and in fact appear to be substantially outdated, there is no compulsory insurance, the compensation ceilings are insufficient and the liability systems require that the victim be the one to provide proof that it is the fault of the carrier and this is a difficult proof to provide in the event of a shipwreck. in view of this, the commission saw only one solution: the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the programme. this is about implementing the athens convention. the negotiations are being conducted under the auspices of the imo and are being fully implemented in order to ensure that all victims receive compensation under the conditions and within the limits set by the convention. the council has shown that it is of the same opinion. all the amendments tabled by the european parliament are intended to give new meaning to the future regulation. so we support them wholeheartedly. as regards the scope of application, which must be as broad as possible, it cannot be denied that some national or river transport operators are experiencing difficulties. it would therefore be legitimate to implement the regulation in stages over time to allow for the necessary adjustments. i therefore support the amendments. at present, the maximum compensation depends on the size of the ship and the number of victims, and this is not acceptable. this must be remedied, inter alia, by making life insurance easier by setting a single european-wide ceiling for compensation. that is the subject of amendments nos 12, 13 and 14, part one, which the commission supports. i am extending my speech, mr president, because i think it is right to give an opinion on the various amendments which have been tabled, so if you will allow me, i will take two more minutes. as regards the vlasto report on port state control, i thank the rapporteur and parliament for supporting the proposal which will lead to the implementation of an ambitious new inspection regime for europe. i would like to make two comments on two essential aspects: the first concerns the mechanisms under which the conditions for inspections of ships cannot be determined. on the one hand, there is the flexibility, which is justified for operational reasons and is already provided for in the current directive, so we believe that it should be maintained. for this reason, i cannot give my favourable opinion on amendments nos 19 and 23. the most important aspect from a political point of view is the ban on the use of the products referred to in amendments nos 31 and 32. if the commission can accept the council's view that a less stringent regime should be introduced for ships on the grey list, i am glad that parliament supports the commission on the issue of permanent ban. as regards the de grandes pascual report on classification societies, i am pleased that parliament has accepted the division of the act into directives and regulations, as requested by the council, which seems to me to be a fair and rigorous approach from a legal point of view. as regards the amendments, i would say that amendments nos 27 and 28 introduce changes in the civil liability regime of recognised bodies and we find them to be incoherent. in any event, death due to negligence must continue to be covered by the directive and be covered by minimum liability. as regards amendment no 1, which deletes the third recital which the council added to the draft regulation, we can accept it. this recital seems to us to be superfluous and dangerous; i would not want to see our inspectors having a hard time doing their job because of it. finally, as i have said, i can accept the amendments to incorporate into the draft directive certain elements from the flag state proposal. i am sorry, mr president, that i have been a little long, but there were so many amendments and i thought it was right to let the house know what the commission's view was.

president of the council. - mr president, thank you very much, ladies and gentlemen, for this very exciting debate. we could sit here for hours because the subject is indeed worth a great deal of debate and the reflections you have given are exciting, but unfortunately we are short of time. the lessons i have learned are as follows: firstly, as regards the position on laissez-faire, on the absence of regulation, i believe that, in view of the reservations which are due to my office, i have been quite clear. it seems to me that the debate between 'regulation' and 'no regulation' must be overcome. financial deregulation is now an archaic concept. strong, modern financial regulation is the solution for the future. it must be adapted, we must go beyond what has been done so far. that is the first point, and from that point of view i am very clear. i listened carefully to what mrs koch-mehrin also said and i take up what she said, namely that regulation is not the enemy of the market. we all have our responsibilities. it is up to the public authorities to regulate, to adapt the regulations, because what is at stake is the stability of a system, the protection of small savers, the protection of depositors. i also say to mr wurtz that it is also employment, growth and the impact on the real economy that are at stake in this crisis today, and that is why action must be taken, including for the most modest, and quickly. secondly, europe must act in the context of closer international cooperation. there's no other choice. europe, it has been said, must make its voice heard, otherwise - i was going to say as usual - we shall suffer what we deserve from american regulations. we have already done this with sarbane-oxley, we have seen the effects it had on a number of european companies, we have seen what it has done to accounting standards and market standards. we can start again today. the only advantage is that europe now has the opportunity to make its voice heard on the international stage, as commissioner almunia has said, as the president of the european union - president sarkozy - has done, to take the lead, to be ahead of the game. i really call on europeans to coordinate their efforts to ensure that the union has a strong presence on the international scene and to reflect on the international financial architecture and on the international regulatory bodies. because if no international action is taken, we will not have to complain that we have no other choice but to call on sovereign funds, which we would like to keep. i am not making any judgments, but we must have some consistency in this respect, we must know what we want to do and if europe does not act, we will also be dependent on other funds to stabilise the financial system. third conviction: this has been mentioned by many, including president schulz. it is true that we have to raise the problem of remuneration and the problem of earnings which are linked to cyclical market activities. the problem of the remuneration of market operators must also be seen in the context of this international reflection. i'm not the first to say it, gordon brown said it in his day. it seems to me that this is a logical and thoroughly considered matter. it is clear that this is not just an economic and financial crisis, it is also an ethical crisis, a crisis of responsibility. this is a crisis of economic ethics and it challenges all actors and all policy-makers, regardless of their sensitivity. as has been stressed, finance must remain at the service of the economy and the economy must not be the victim of finance, as has also been emphasized by mr wurtz and other speakers in this field. as i said, we must reflect on the role of the financial institutions and on the road map which has been drawn up by the finance ministers with the support of the commission, on the basis of proposals from the commission. let us talk about concrete progress: i say to pervenche berès, we must go further and we must act quickly in terms of timetable. commissioner almunia said - i take him at his word - that the commission must be able to act very quickly because what is at stake, and i would like to end on that, is the restoration of confidence. the important thing is that, even though europe is less affected, we were sending messages of confidence. messages of confidence mean action, international cooperation, not being afraid to adapt regulations, acting quickly and putting proposals on the table in the run-up to the european council on 15 october, making use of the proposals of your assembly and, as has been said, being attentive to the fact that we are also facing movements which affect not only liquidity - that has been said - but also the solvency of the whole financial system. from that point forward, economic confidence will be the key to rebuilding growth, and that is why we must act with extreme vigour, without dogmatism, and we must use the full range of instruments at our disposal.
member of the commission. − mr president, i agree with all those who have stressed in this debate that we have to react; that we have to react to a very big transformation in our financial system; that we need to learn from the errors of the past; and that we need to work together – the european institutions – because, without our interinstitutional cooperation, we all know that we cannot succeed. we also need, in reacting, to work together with the other players in this game, and we know that we are talking about global financial systems. if they were not global, we would not be affected in the way we are, so we cannot forget that our leadership, our initiatives and our decisions should be followed by a high degree of consensus around our positions with the other partners and the other players. if not – let us be honest – we will pay the price of being clear but naive, and we will not be competitive in the financial industry, and we need to continue to be competitive – not only efficient, not only rigorous, not only able to learn the lessons of the past, but also to be competitive. as i have already said in my introductory remarks – and i agree with the chair’s remarks – what i mean by reaction in the short term is to fully implement the ecofin road map as soon as possible – and we are on track, mrs berès. the assessment carried out a few weeks ago in nice shows that we are on track in adopting the decisions of this ecofin. next week we will need to put forward proposals on the capital requirements directive and, in a few weeks, to the credit rating agencies directive. in this parliament and in the council, the adoption as soon as possible of the solvency ii directive is also very important. but beyond the eu’s borders the financial stability forum needs to continue working very intensively; it is a very important institution at this moment – the level 3 committees of the lamfalussy framework. we are deeply concerned – parliament, the commission and, i hope, also the council – about the lack of efficiency of some reactions at this level, and these are key institutions that should work much more efficiently than when these institutions were created a few years ago – the basel committee, the international accounting standards board – that is a key issue, as mr jouyet said. so, we are not alone. we have to react quickly, in an efficient way, taking into account the big problems that we are facing and, at the same time, ensuring that our leadership is followed by others – as we know is the case in many other regulatory areas. from a structural point of view, unfortunately, we cannot decide on everything today. but it is true – and i fully agree – that the relationship between regulation and markets will change because of this crisis. it is obvious there is a regulatory failure, among things. i think we all agree that we need to establish a more intense relationship at all levels with the us authorities, not only in our task as the commission or the executive branches, but also parliament with congress, which is now a key actor in the solution of the particular problems in the usa. we need to react at the multilateral level. the real origin of all these failures in the financial systems – the excess of liquidity, the excess of risks adopted by the actors, the low risk aversion that we have seen in the past – the cupidité, in the words of mr jouyet – has been created by these global imbalances that the global institutions have not been able to solve so far, and we need to act, as europeans united, to convince the other partners in the global arena that, if we are not able to adjust these global imbalances in an orderly way, they will create new problems in the future, and we need to coordinate ourselves within the eu in a more clear and efficient way. we are living in an economic and monetary union. we have an internal market, we have an action plan for integration of financial services, but we still have a lot of internal barriers and inefficiency. i think all of us should be aware that this will require more european integration and not more national reactions or defensive attitudes from the member states. beyond this, we need to keep in mind what our challenges are for the medium to long term, and we need to preserve, in this very difficult environment, the stability and growth pact, the lisbon strategy, and the energy and climate change strategies, which are extremely important now. we cannot afford to forget that we are facing not only very difficult short-term challenges from the point of view of financial markets, but also big challenges over the medium to long term for the world economy and for our own future. one last word: this was not in the road map but will be on the agenda of the next ecofin, and the commission will fully agree with this issue. we need to think about the systems of remuneration of executives, directors and ceos and all those who can create trends and who can adopt decisions in the markets. i will tell you one thing – and this is also addressed to the council – in 2004 the commission – and in particular my colleague charlie mccreevy – put forward a recommendation asking the member states to adopt decisions in this regard, to avoid wrong incentives. we have been considering what has happened since then, during the last four years. only one out of the 27 member states reacted positively to this recommendation from the commission point of view. so the commission fully agrees now with this consensus to touch upon these important issues as well.
the debate is closed. the written declaration (article 142)

member of the commission. − madam president, first i would like to thank the honourable member of parliament for his congratulations, but i would like to pass his congratulations on to parliament, because parliament, in a very difficult situation with five directives on the table on very complicated matters, has done a wonderful job. i might not agree 100% on everything parliament has voted, but what parliament has done today is put the single market for telecoms on the agenda. now the council has to look at what parliament has proposed and try to find a common way in order to make this telecom package become a reality for industry and consumers. with regard to the question on roaming, is there not a risk that, because we bring down prices on roaming, the operators try to raise prices in another way? we already heard last year, when we introduced the voice roaming package, that the operators would be forced to raise the national cost for voice mobiles, but what we saw was just the contrary. so what happened? firstly, citizens, instead of switching off their phones when they are abroad, are now using them. so the volume on voice has gone up tremendously, by 34% in one year only. secondly, because there is competition at national level, national prices have not risen but have gone down by 10-12%. the honourable member recalls the polemics which were going on at a certain time about ‘bill and keep’. it is up to the operators what kind of billing system they want to adopt. our european way of doing it is not to use ‘bill and keep’. that is the american way of doing it. i have just seen that prices in the united states are lower than prices here, and i told the operator very clearly that they should choose their business model. it is not for the commissioner to do that, but they have to be on terms with their customers. the only thing that concerns me is that there is transparency, that prices do not go above price limits which are unacceptable, and that all european consumers can feel at home when they are travelling in europe and when they are communicating in europe. regarding the question on inadvertent roaming: yes, we are aware of this. coming from luxembourg, you can imagine how many complaints i receive from consumers on this question, because some luxembourgers living in a border area have one operator in the living room, another one in the kitchen and a third in the bedroom, so i am fully aware of this question. that is why we have raised this question with the national regulators, and we are monitoring this problem with the european regulators group. we will also continue to do so with the national regulators. we have also increased the transparency initiatives for data and sms on the package which is now on the table in the european parliament. there have already been some positive developments concerning this inadvertent roaming, for instance in ireland, with good work done on both sides of the border. i think that is a positive way to see it, and i think that the operators also should be very conscious of the fact of inadvertent roaming. even if it is only a very small percentage of the population which suffers as a result of this question, it is the responsibility of the operators to try to solve the problem.

member of the commission. − i am at the disposal of the honourable mr crowley if he would like to speak with me later on and has a supplementary question. as for the question concerning the break in transmission of the chinese tv channel ntdtv, the commission was very much aware of this problem, and therefore asked eutelsat to clarify the situation. we received a letter from eutelsat which answered that the irreversible loss of one of the v5’s two solar panels has been confirmed both by eutelsat and by the satellite manufacturer, thales space. to safeguard the satellite’s operation, eutelsat switched off the four transponders providing direct-to-home television services while keeping the 20 remaining transponders used for telecommunication services. as eutelsat does not operate any other satellite with coverage of asia, they have provided their customers, including the service provider of ntdtv, with a list of competitor satellites with appropriate coverage and availability capacity. eutelsat also pointed out that their satellites carried channels representing all channels, cultures and political viewpoints. they refrain from indulging in the slightest judgement as to the ideological and political positioning of the channels. eutelsat reaffirmed to the commission that they had not taken any action against ntdtv at the behest of the government of china or anyone else. ntdtv is actually still carried by one of their european satellites. eutelsat also supplied technical information showing that, in order to receive ntdtv, rather large satellite dishes were necessary, which made it unlikely that a significant part of the population of the people’s republic of china could receive it.
member of the commission. − concerning the first question, eutelsat has told us that the breakdown is irreversible and that the transmission of tv services cannot be resumed. so it is a purely technical question. unfortunately, the capacity is only 50%, so the energy which can be taken up is only 50%. it is a technical question which, unfortunately, cannot be solved. now to the more fundamental question from the honourable member as to whether we should, some day, have a ‘europe without borders’ for television. we are not yet there. we have our television without frontiers directive, which is now implemented in an audiovisual services without frontiers directive, where i hope very much that the video-on-demand services can become europe-wide services. the dream, of course, is that one day there will no longer be any borders and that citizens, wherever they are, can receive whatever tv channels they want. we are not yet there because the selling of rights is still done under a national system. one day, europe will arrive at a situation where the selling of rights can also be done at a european level. i favour this. i cannot impose it, but i favour it, and i believe that slowly but surely we will move beyond the national selling of rights to the european selling of rights.
member of the commission. −the european commission's new strategy on multilingualism, entitled 'multilingualism, a benefit for europe and a common commitment', was adopted on 18 september 2008. the main theme of the strategy is linguistic diversity and how best to use and develop it in order to foster intercultural dialogue, boost the competitiveness of european companies and improve skills and employability for european citizens. the strategy therefore focuses on encouraging the use and learning of foreign languages in the member states rather than on the internal language regime of the european institutions. the commitment to developing citizens' ability to communicate in two languages in addition to their mother tongue is reaffirmed, while at the same time the need to provide citizens with a wider range of languages to enable them to learn those foreign languages in which they have a greater interest is highlighted. the commission will draw on existing community programmes, in particular the lifelong learning programme, to support member states in promoting foreign languages through the implementation of this strategy. under council regulation no 1 of 15 april 1958, as amended by article 1 of council regulation no 920/2005 of 13 june 2005, irish acquired the status of an official language and working language of the institutions of the european union with effect from 1 january 2007. however, articles 2 and 3 of the regulation provide for a partial derogation, renewable every five years, concerning the use of the irish language by the institutions of the european union. in practice, this derogation implies that, for the time being, only proposals for regulations under the codecision procedure and certain related documents, as well as direct correspondence with the public, are translated into or from irish. in this respect, in accordance with the provisions mentioned above, the commission was able to carry out all the translations into irish necessary for the legislative process and to ensure their timely transmission. in addition, replies to questions addressed to the commission by citizens or legal persons were provided in irish. in addition to the obligations arising from the amended regulation 1 and within the limits of the resources available, the commission has also started to present some of its high profile webpages in irish, giving priority to content of particular interest to irish-speaking citizens. as regards interpretation, the directorate-general for interpretation is in a position to respond to all requests for interpretation, in and from irish, received from the council, the commission or the committees and will continue to make efforts to ensure that it has sufficient resources to do the same in the future.
member of the commission. − looking at the requirements that were put before the european commission, we can say with satisfaction that they were not only met, but that the european commission went beyond them. on the other hand, to promote and encourage the wider use of the irish language at community level, it is a joint effort of both the community institutions and, above all, the irish authorities and society, i will give you just one example: in this respect, we need, in order to ensure wider use of the irish language, more speakers, more translators, and without adequate training, without allocating significant resources at the national level, that is, at the irish level, it will be difficult to achieve this. this is why i am in close contact with the irish authorities to encourage and stimulate those who wish to do so to come and train and acquire the knowledge necessary to work at the level of the community institutions in the field of languages. i would also like to stress that we are in close contact with the irish authorities not only on institutional matters but also on the various developments in the irish language. of course, we want to help with all our strengths the development of, for example, terminology at the level of the irish language and, as i told you, we have very close links, not only with the authorities but, in general, with all the actors who are involved in the field.
member of the commission. − the european commission internship programme is open to anyone who has completed university studies, who has not yet completed an internship with the european institutions and who has a thorough knowledge of at least one of the european commission's working languages: german, english or french. this is a practical requirement that allows a trainee to participate in the activities of the services and to benefit fully from the traineeship. in addition, practical information and explanations to help applicants are available only in these three languages. moreover, the provisions on the traineeship programme are available on the europa website in all the official languages of the union, in force at the date of adoption of the commission's reference decision. in order to fulfil the task laid down in article 177 of the ec treaty, the number of languages in which the proposals of the european instrument for democracy and human rights may be accepted should be limited to those languages which are understood and used on a regular basis in the third countries concerned. however, documents submitted by non-governmental organisations in support of their proposals for external aid projects, such as their status documents, are now accepted in all official languages of the union through pador, the online registration system for non-governmental organisations. for awareness raising or coordination actions taking place exclusively in the union and where the main target groups are union citizens, applications submitted in the language (s) of the member state (s) concerned will be assessed. the first page of the online anti-discrimination campaign uses an english logo, but it provides access to web pages in almost all the official languages of the union. in line with the action plan for better communication with citizens, in 2006 the commission set up a web translation service within the translation directorate. the commission has thus progressively increased its multilingual communication capacity through the translation of web pages. however, given the rapid evolution of the internet and the need to fulfil first its legal translation obligations arising from the requirements of regulation no 1, the commission must constantly strike the right balance between the option of making relevant and up-to-date information available to union stakeholders and the option of ensuring full multilingualism for all commission websites. with regard to the use of languages on web pages, the general principle is to adapt the language regime of each website to the target audience. the commission therefore ensures that the websites or parts of the websites of interest to all citizens are translated into as many official languages as possible, while more technical topics of interest mainly to specialists are presented in a limited number of languages or only in the language of the text. similarly, information that is generally expected to remain for a longer period will be published in more languages than more temporary content. the commission's obligations under regulation no 1 imply, on the one hand, that regulations and directives, as well as all legislative proposals and communications formally approved by the commission and sent to the institutions, are translated into all the official languages and, on the other hand, that replies to letters from citizens are drafted in the language of their choice. in addition to these obligations, and in accordance with the principle of multilingualism and multiculturalism, the commission is committed to making every effort to ensure equal treatment of citizens, cultures and languages.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, before we begin the debate on the report we are voting on tomorrow morning, i should like to take this opportunity to express my sincere thanks. i would like to begin by thanking my colleague, now senator of the italian republic, adriana poli bortone, from whom i inherited the draft report and an already careful and thorough study of the problem; i would like to thank my colleagues who have worked with me in carrying out the in-depth study and analysis of the phenomenon with enthusiasm and dedication, and the shadow rapporteurs, who have undoubtedly contributed with their commitment to the implementation of the text in the committee on the environment, with political and practically unanimous agreement. ladies and gentlemen, when i was given the task of this project, i asked myself what my objective as rapporteur should be in carrying out a study of this kind, and i found an answer in the strategic nature of the document which indicated the two pillars on which i should base my work: the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's financial instruments are not used to the detriment of the community's own resources. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for adoption by the end of the year. in undertaking this journey, i relied on data, statistics, percentages, which are already widely available on the subject. and that's a disturbing number, because if you look at the world health organization, more than a billion people are overweight, and more than 300 million people are obese. obesity in children is growing very rapidly and it is estimated that obesity and overweight-related diseases account for up to 6% of national health expenditure in some member states. in our search for solutions, we have been careful not to demonize certain food categories as the sole cause of obesity. it is not by eliminating these foods from the diet that the problem is solved, but rather by educating the consumer citizen and especially the young, the child, in proper nutrition. fats are essential for proper nutrition, but in the right amounts and at the right times of the day. the food pedagogy on which i insist strongly is not the ability to discern good food from bad, nothing is bad, absolutely nothing and in health conditions, unless dietary related pathologies, must be excluded from the diet. another problem i want to draw your attention to: obesity is a disease. a disease with causes not only physical but often social or psychological, but still a disease which imposes huge costs on our national health systems every year. as such, it must be tackled with concrete, multi-level solutions. in these months of study, however, i have come to realize that too often the public underestimates this aspect, wasting time in very justified alarms and awareness campaigns against anorexia but in an equally unjust consolatory approach to overweight with slogans such as: fat is good, and so on. this is wrong, it's uneducational; we're not talking about aesthetics or looks, we're talking about health. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work is a good one. we call on the educators, the health professionals, the food industry, the media, particularly television, to feel the strong sense of responsibility attached to their potential to shape public opinion. the public administration, in particular, and the local administration. i would like to conclude, ladies and gentlemen, with a piece of news that has been circulating for some days: one of the two candidates for the white house has argued that it would be useful, right, necessary to tax obese citizens the same way we tax alcoholics and smokers. we believe that we are facing an absurdity in principle, but we believe it is essential that this serious inconvenience and this serious problem be dealt with in the right way, because only with a method that can lead us to determine certain conditions can a positive result be achieved.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on his excellent work. i shall of course repeat many of the points made by my colleagues, but i do not think we should use half-words. obesity affects approximately 25% of european children and is therefore a serious risk to their future health. the causes include poor information, poor dietary habits, lack of physical activity, even lack of sports facilities. social and psychological problems are not to be underestimated either, since overweight children are often the victims of bullying. i therefore find the proposal to increase funding for the school fruit scheme, which provides free fruit and vegetables on the school shelves, interesting. the 2009 mediterranean diet and fruit and vegetable production should be revived, even in the face of the latest who data which show that mediterranean countries are also experiencing a decline in the consumption of this type of food. this initiative will use fruit, which was previously destroyed to maintain prices, to ensure healthier food, especially for our children, and thus a healthier future for european citizens.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to emphasize something which i consider very important, particularly in view of the statements made by the commissioner, namely that he has focused his attention on a problem which must be tackled seriously, while also seeking to provide opportunities. i think that this is a subject which many of us are interested in, because there have been a number of speeches, all of them specific, they have dealt with the subject, they have tried to point out and urge the commission, but above all the report, to achieve an objective which is to establish a principle which we certainly have a great criticism, which is that of obesity. obesity, in the context of the health problem, which is a problem that is becoming extremely complicated because it has to be solved, because it has to be helped, because it has to be tried to establish a relationship that has to lead us to achieve our goals. so i think, commissioner, that it is also essential to think that the commission has emphasized the role of the world health organization, but it is the world health organization that is asking for the trend of increasing childhood obesity to be reversed by 2015. but in 2010 we will have an important date, which is to actually establish what we have achieved with regard to this strategy. so, i think, in thanking all of the speakers, the shadow speakers, but all of the suggestions that have been there, in saying that we have to be very careful, observers in trying to establish an important relationship that can allow us to really think about prevention and balance to eat well, not just in the body, but also in the mind and soul; and i believe that we can really achieve this by everyone working together. again, thank you to all those who have spoken in support of our report. thank you, chief.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in europe four out of every 100 citizens go abroad for treatment. i believe that health migration is a thermometer of a territorial dysfunction, a lack of services. for italians who seek treatment in other countries, the health service spends about 40 million euros a year, in addition to what is obviously private insurance. let us see what the reasons are: the long waiting times for services, that's for sure! an example of this is the 300 days it takes for a prostate operation in italy or the month or more often required for a ct scan. the second reason, of course, is that services are paid for in italy and not in other countries, such as dental care and plastic surgery. a third reason - and i would like to draw everyone's attention to this - is that people go abroad to take advantage of techniques which are prohibited or partially prohibited in their own country, such as artificial insemination, or which are absolutely illegal, such as the purchase of organs from living people. the example in india is sad, but sad examples of this were perhaps also seen in some countries before they joined the union. in short, the quality and cost-effectiveness of the services provided are attractive to therapeutic trips, but in many cases, in my view, there is a need for greater supervision by the union of these services, in order to guarantee consumers and a level playing field. the social context in which the service is provided, even in the new member states, is often a mixture of public and private sectors, and i would recommend, mrs vassiliou, that in addition to the principles you have mentioned, strict monitoring be carried out of the existing rules requiring the use of raw materials, the ce marking and the documents of conformity, because the safety of medical devices and treatments must be guaranteed. let's not forget that there's always someone.... the president will withdraw the floor.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, several very serious and important issues have been raised. first of all i would like to remind you that the european schools system is a completely independent body. it is based not on the treaty of 1958 but on the statute of 1953, it has its own board, its own statute, and all rules are adopted by this board. the commission is only one voice on the board. as for the content of the education, this is fully the responsibility of the board, and all this, including the different proportions between the language sections, and the curriculum, is totally in the hands of the board of governors of the european schools. so the commission has not very much to say. as to financing, this is the second thing i would like to say in reply to one important question. the infrastructure is provided by the host countries. so the schools are built by belgium, germany, france etc. this gives us the full picture of the limits we have in developing the infrastructure. what about the content of education? the honourable member mentioned in her introductory remarks that the quality of the education is high – and it is high. this is one of the main priorities of the european commission, to give every possible support so that this quality will be high. this will really be a benchmark for european educational systems, that european schools give pupils an education which is highly appreciated everywhere. so i do not have any information that pupils with a european school education have any specific difficulties in getting to university after school if they so wish. concerning teachers, they count as part of the infrastructure, so teachers are also provided by member states. english teachers, for example, are provided by the united kingdom; in other words, the burden for bigger languages is correspondingly much higher. we, the commission – or the european budget – pay the operational costs for this. this gives us a combination that results in a rather cumbersome system, and one objective is therefore to reform the system and to bring more clarity to responsibility and financing. you can also see the problems with belgium, where, it has been said, one of the four schools is still a temporary school. the construction of the fourth school has been postponed and postponed, and we are in intensive discussions with the belgian government about this. on the openness of european schools, in our view the key issue is the european baccalaureate, and the certification of schools which want to award the european baccalaureate. we promote this idea, which has basically been adopted by the board of governors, so the basic rules exist. now the question is how to put this into practice in the member states. again, the leading role lies with the member states. so this will to some extent settle the problem of different pupils. today, as i said, i am meeting parliament and i hear your observations that category iii is something which must be excluded, but i also regularly meet our staff – it is the same size, comprising hundreds of people – and they of course have a clear demand, namely that education for their children must be guaranteed. so there is a requirement – and this is emphasised very strongly in the treaty, in the staff regulations, in the regulation – to provide places in the schools and then, of course, the question arises who will distribute these other places which are to remain free and definitely in brussels? this is more and more difficult. this is for me a very complicated question. at the beginning of this commission, we insisted on behalf of our staff that there must be more clarity, and so the central enrolment authority has been established by the board of governors to settle these questions. so this is the overall picture, and i must just repeat that the commission’s attitude is that we must bring clarity to the financial issues and clearly share the burden, have clear responsibilities, clear obligations, and then we can also find better solutions to the infrastructure questions, but we cannot have any kind of reduction in the quality of education. about some specific questions, one honourable member raised the question about disabled students. you said that there are many more of them but i do not know that anybody has been rejected when parents have asked for special treatment: it has always been provided. so, if you have facts that there are some hidden pupils with disabilities, please provide these facts and we will deal with them. now, about parliamentary assistants, you know that at present parliamentary assistants are not covered by the staff regulations, they are a kind of special staff members in parliament, but you know also that negotiations are ongoing to settle this and to have more precise rules, and then we can also consider what to do about access to the european schools for the children of parliamentary assistants. so these are more or less the questions which were raised, and of course all these questions – religious education, languages – are clearly in the hands of the board of governors, and the commission is just one voice on that board. the board of governors is dealing with these issues very seriously. they have held long discussions about this, and i can assure you that the secretariat-general of the european schools is very attentive to all needs of the different languages and different religious aspects. so this is their responsibility. just one thing more: if parliament can draw member states’ attention, and especially if all members of the european parliament who have their own connections in their home countries can encourage the member states’ ministers of education, to promote this idea of the european baccalaureate because this is their choice. we now have rules on how to go ahead with the european baccalaureate. now it is up to the national ministries to find interested schools. i know that there are a lot of interested schools, but the national authorities in many countries have not shown enough enthusiasm about this project, which can be a step forward and which can really then be a positive mark for the european baccalaureate, so we can have european schools not only in brussels but everywhere – in new member states and old member states. this is a symbol of europe. the baccalaureate and european education is one element in our architecture.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we are in full agreement with what president sarkozy said in evian: only coordinated action by central banks and governments will contain systemic risk. this does not mean that, despite the interesting debate today, we still have some disturbing doubts as to why the european central bank did not lower interest rates earlier than what was happening on the american market, on the world market and on the financial market of some countries of the european union. we wonder why there has been no clear position on the derivatives problem, when we know that this product has exponentially indebted some important public institutions and public administrations in italy and europe. we wonder why the policy of consolidating banking institutions has continued, creating clay giants on many occasions without taking account of the real system we have within our countries, and why consumer credit has not been controlled, thus creating exponential indebtedness both on the part of individuals and, in turn, on the part of banking institutions. finally, we ask that europe today have the courage to revise the stability pact, which is now a thing of the past century. in the face of new and exponential crises, decisions must be made quickly and with certainty. the council must also make it clear, since we have been talking about small and mediumsized enterprises, that the commission has a duty to bring down the cost of fuel more significantly.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, europe has not protected the people from financial speculation. even in the new york times we read the prophetic verse of the poet pound: "with usury no one has a stable home". today the fed and the us treasury want to cure crack by lowering rates. a medicine easy credit that caused the speculative bubbles. in 1933 a group of chicago economists proposed a plan: the government should be given back the exclusive monopoly on the issuance of money, banking institutions should be prohibited from creating fake money, and banks should be required to maintain 100% reserve requirements. so fractional-credit fraud is impossible, no more financial games that ruin the poor, the savers, the real economy! the nobel prize winner maurice allais has long been railing against innovative finance, securitisations, derivatives and hedge funds, which are so popular with a certain financial europe, the gnomes of finance. he rightly calls for - as we have been calling for - a ban on derivatives. we're going to go with the chicago plan, the allais plan. the creation of money for the states only. enough with europe uncertain of its course, rightly warned by the pope. money is not everything, it's nothing!

author of the book. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, our colleague from the previous legislature, maurizio turco, now a radical member of the italian parliament, had lodged an application - an application as a citizen can lodge - seeking access to council documents in which the names of the national delegations which had taken certain positions during the debate had been censored, as had access to a legal opinion and the request had been refused by the council. the action before the court of first instance, which had in the meantime urged the council to make the identity of the national delegations accessible in order to prevent the court from ruling on the matter, had proved turco wrong and the council right. however, the appeal to the court of justice has reversed the situation. the court simply said that access to documents, and in particular to those with legislative effects, must be compulsory, because access to documents is democracy and any exception is to be interpreted in an extremely limited way, there being an obvious public interest. public and legal debate on documents can give further legitimacy to the institutions and improve self-confidence. the question we ask today in summary is: how do the commission and the european institutions intend to follow up this judgment? that is to say, it should also be an opportunity for a thorough review of the operational methods of immediate publication of documents. i know very well that this is simply a citizen's appeal, as any citizen could have done, and not a reform followed by an institutional debate. but i say, all the more so, that this is the strength of maurizio turco's initiative, which shows how the individual case can do perhaps much more than what institutional initiatives offer us. we need to maximize the publicity of these documents. we must know that, for example, just today at the european commission press conference it was confirmed that the commission has not yet asked the italian government for information on a matter which maurizio turco himself raised on discrimination in the teaching of religion in our country. why hasn't this been requested? it is a concrete example of the mechanisms by which the functioning of the european institutions becomes inscrutable to the citizen. so let's seize this opportunity for a radical and profound reform of access and disclosure of documents.
author of the book. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the presidency of the council has mentioned the amount of one million documents published. in the case of access to documents, quantity is also quality, but it is not only quality. if we look closely, there's a problem of what kind of documents: the minutes of the meeting or documents accompanying the formulation of decisions. that's what's missing today. let me give you an example. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european parliament is not forced to take part in the negotiations on the new treaty, and that the council is not forced to take part in the negotiations on the new treaty. i just gave an example with the few seconds of time. i believe that, even in the light of the answers we have received, this occasion should be seen more as an opportunity than as a risk to the functioning of the european institutions.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am trying to make up for lost time, because it seems to me that it is a little late. i would like to thank the committees that have expressed their views and the shadow rapporteurs with whom we have worked over the past few months. it is also thanks to their contribution that we have drawn up a text which has allowed us to have a large majority in the committee on employment. we have thus shown that the fight against undeclared work is a problem which affects all countries and which requires europe to take a concrete stance in this fight if the objectives set out in lisbon are to be achieved. the text has adopted points which i consider to be very important on a subject such as underwater work, which is of great importance: the commission has already made a number of proposals. this means that there is a widespread situation of illegality which cannot be tolerated because it in fact causes a serious disturbance of competition between firms and territories and makes work and those who do it less safe in all respects. it is therefore right to draw attention to this, to make people more aware that the absence of a serious fight against undeclared work is likely to generate these problems and, at the same time, to seriously undermine the social security systems in europe in the near future. we have started from these considerations to draw up this proposal which is being submitted to parliament. as i said, there are important points in the report which, if the commission also makes a real effort, can lead to positive results, proposals which we consider useful. in doing so i think i can say that the european parliament has done its part and that it is now up to the other institutional bodies to do their part to achieve the objectives of combating undeclared work.
in writing. health is a commodity that has a cost but no price. investment in health is the most effective and efficient investment for a society of human scale. and this investment is a shared responsibility of the individual who must activate healthy lifestyles by holding their own behaviours accountable, of the healthcare staff who must preserve their sense of professional ethics, of the national and regional governments who must pay particular attention to the sustainability of healthcare systems. particular attention should also be paid to the need for integrated health and social policies to respond to new needs. combating inequalities, addressing the demanding demand for health, the epidemiological changes taking place, and increasingly effective cooperation between the member states and the regions are requirements which the rapporteur, mr peterle, has understood well and for which i thank him for the excellent work he has done.

in writing. - i vote in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the situation in belarus following the parliamentary elections of 28 september 2008. despite the considerable signs of openness on the part of the belarusian authorities, such as the release of political prisoners and the refusal to recognise the unilaterally declared independence of south ossetia and abkhazia, i believe that the democratic legitimacy of the elections just held is at least questionable. this is the result of an internal policy which is in no way aligned with that of the european union: the death penalty and the application of certain articles of the penal code as a means of repression are proof of this. the belarusian government must therefore make every effort to ensure genuinely democratic elections in accordance with international law in the future.
in writing. - i give my vote in favour of the motion for a resolution on the suspension of the doha round of negotiations of the world trade organisation. i am fully aware of the difficulties involved in trying to reach a single result in the negotiations. i believe that the difficulties in the doha negotiations highlight the need for reform within the wto, to ensure transparency and effectiveness which have not been achieved so far. i also stress the need to create, within the framework of the doha development agenda, technical assistance aimed at helping the developing countries. finally, i am convinced that in the present context a positive conclusion to the doha treaties can be a stabilizing factor for the whole world economy.
in writing. - i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on introducing the symbols of the union in the regulation after they were surprisingly excluded from the new treaty. as a member of the european convention, i have always said that the union needs a soul which, through shared common values, brings it closer to the citizens of europe. the exclusion of symbols from the treaty was yet another act of alienation of the european institutions from the citizens. how can we expect the latter to be recognised in the union if the union is becoming increasingly unrecognizable, even losing the symbols that should represent it, both in the member states and in its international relations? the recognition by all of the symbols of the union is a first step towards that commonality of intentions for the construction of a common european home capable not only of giving political answers to the european citizens but also of restoring to politics the primacy which it deserves in the understanding and management of the 'public good'. i therefore renew my congratulations to the rapporteur in the hope that this initiative of the european parliament will find a response in the other european institutions and in the conviction that it will strengthen the parliamentary institution of which we are a part.
in writing. - i give my vote in favour of the report by mr carnero gonzález on the insertion in the rules of procedure of the european parliament of a new article on the use by parliament of the symbols of the union. the symbols is known are worth more than any slogan or word: they are indispensable components of any kind of communication, especially those relating to the processes of identification in a social group or organisation. flags, effigies, anthems are essential if an organisation is to be recognised as such by public opinion. i therefore welcome the initiative of my colleague, which is aimed at facilitating the participation and communication of citizens in the european project, thereby contributing to its legitimacy.

member of the commission. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i shall first try to answer mrs gebhardt's report and then i shall answer the oral question which you very appropriately linked to the report. i welcome president deprez, who is also present. i would like to thank you very much, mrs gebhardt, for your excellent report and for the excellent cooperation you have had with the commission on this sensitive and sensitive subject. the rome iii proposal is very important to us and not just to the commission - i know it is of great interest to the european parliament - and i believe it is important in supporting the free movement of people within the european union. i would remind you, madam president, of some of the data available: we currently have 2 200 000 marriages every year in the european union, of which 350 000 are international marriages! that's already a lot, 350,000 international marriages. obviously, this phenomenon will increase. the proposal affects about 170 000 divorces each year, or about 19% of the total of some 875 000 divorces annually in the european union. 20% is a significant figure! that is why the commission shares your view, madam president, on the importance of the rome iii proposal. this proposal brings more predictability, legal certainty for the couples concerned. you mentioned it - in the absence of devices - we either have forum shopping, or it is the stronger partner of the couple who wins. the commission therefore broadly endorses the european parliament's report on the original rome iii proposal, subject to certain reservations. the commission supports parliament's amendments to ensure that the choice of spouse is an informed one. the commission agrees with parliament that the formal conditions for the conclusion of marriage contracts should be made more stringent and that the weaker spouses should be protected. but we must also take account of the differences between the legal systems of the member states in this area. it is not a question of harmonizing, as you have just pointed out. in the same vein, the commission welcomes parliament's proposals to improve public information on national and european laws on marriage and divorce contracts. there is one point on which we differ: the commission does not think it necessary to include a new jurisdictional criterion based on the place of marriage. the link between the place of the marriage ceremony and the situation of the couple at the time of separation may be very tenuous. however, the commission agrees with parliament's amendment on the possibility for spouses to bring the matter before the court of last resort when the divorce cannot be pronounced by the court of their habitual residence. but we're looking at it as an exceptional hypothesis. the commission also prefers to leave the interpretation of the concept of 'habitual residence of the spouses' to the court of justice because this concept already appears in a number of legal instruments and, at the moment, no formal definition has been given. national judges seem to apply it without too much difficulty. we believe that, in order to respect the diversity of the legal systems of the member states, we can trust the court of justice. nor do we see the need to limit rome iii to the law of the member states alone. this is an important question. the member states want to be able to continue to apply the divorce laws of third countries which share our democratic values: for example, if a german or a french woman marries a swiss man, it is easy to think that the same rules we give ourselves should also be able to apply to this union, to this disunion. but be careful! the commission agrees with parliament that an anti-discrimination clause must be included in rome iii, of course, allowing any european court to rule out the application of foreign laws which are incompatible with the principle of equality between spouses. with this anti-discrimination clause, we can probably apply it to couples such as switzerland/member state or norway/member state. i now turn to the question of how to make rome iii a success and i thank mrs gebhardt and mr deprez again for the oral question on the progress of the rome iii dossier. of course, i share your regret that the negotiations on the rome iii dossier have been blocked at council level. we had a debate last july between the ministers of justice on the possibility of using enhanced cooperation in rome iii and, at the end of july, nine member states, more than a third of the member states involved in the adoption of rome iii, submitted a request to the commission for enhanced cooperation. so obviously the commission must look into this request for enhanced cooperation. but you will see that in this too, in order to succeed, it is necessary to be attentive to the whole context. i will now answer the three questions you have put to the commission. first of all, i should like to say that a possible withdrawal of the commission's original rome iii proposal is not on the agenda. if the commission agrees to make a proposal to the council on enhanced cooperation in the field of rome iii, when the decision is taken, it may nevertheless, in the interests of legal clarity, withdraw its original proposal in order to amend it. but that is if we have the possibility of engaging in closer cooperation. in any case, withdrawal is not on the agenda. i take this opportunity to recall briefly the procedure which organizes the mechanism of enhanced cooperation. the commission has to be asked first by at least eight member states, which it is. where this is the case, the application fulfils the other criteria laid down in the treaty on european union compliance with the rules of the internal market , the commission may submit a proposal to the council. if it does not, it shall state the reasons for its failure to submit a proposal. enhanced cooperation must then be authorised by the council, after consulting or assenting to parliament, as appropriate. the request for enhanced cooperation, of course, raises some questions both from a legal and a political point of view. it is necessary to confront the need to continue our joint action on family law as closely as possible to the citizens, to confront this need with the risk of over-fragmenting the european area of justice which could result from a whole series of enhanced cooperation. before i make my statement, i would of course like to hear from the members of parliament and i would very much like the member states to make their position very clear. in any case, i would like to assure the european parliament that i intend, and not only intend, but intend to take judicial cooperation in civil matters in europe forward. family law should not be the poor relation of civil justice. it would be paradoxical, given that these are issues which touch the daily lives of citizens most closely. fortunately, progress has been made in the circulation of divorce decisions, parental responsibility and child visitation rights. i would also like to say that we have texts, but that the commissioner, with your help, must now ensure that these rules are properly applied. i am thinking in particular of the right of access to children and childcare, where not everything is satisfactory in europe at the moment. in short, we could imagine a legislative proposal on the law applicable to this matter... and i would add something: at the same time we are preparing a law applicable to matrimonial regimes, which could be adopted in early 2010. that is the state of the matter, madam president. i cannot, of course, prejudge the consultation which we are about to begin with the member states. what i can say is that the commission clearly wants to move forward, but we must once again ensure that we can get the majority of member states on board. that is a bit my view but i hope, like you and parliament, that things will go forward.
